title: Minimize observability fanout and introduce compact trace-forwarding protocol
creator: Ethan Brooks
description:
Background: Our current observability pipeline fans out every span and metric point to multiple exporters synchronously which creates CPU/memory pressure and increases tail latency in the runtime. This ticket reduces fanout surface area, replaces the verbose wire format between runtime and forwarder with a compact binary-forwarding protocol, and introduces a low-allocation fast-path in the trace proxy to reduce GC pressure under high span rates.

Goals: 
- Reduce p95 trace/metric write CPU by >= 20% under production span rates.
- Reduce runtime GC allocations attributable to observability by >= 30%.
- Cut time-to-first-byte for trace export by >= 25% on burst traffic.
- Maintain existing telemetry semantics (service, span attributes, status) and sampling behavior.

Scope: 
- Implement an opt-in compact protocol between runtime and observability proxy (binary framing + delta-encoding for common attributes).
- Add fanout-throttling: unify exporter fanout to a single forwarder process that multiplexes to external exporters asynchronously.
- Introduce zero-copy buffer pools for span serialization and reuse across requests.
- Add adaptive sampling hook to the forwarder that can collapse duplicate noisy spans at the edge.
- Compatibility shims: runtime will continue to produce OTLP JSON for legacy forwarders until rollout completes.

Implementation plan: 
1) Design phase (this ticket) - schema for compact protocol, edge cases for attribute deltas, backwards compatibility rules. Documented in RFC (link in comments).
2) Prototype - C/Go wire encoder in the runtime to emit compact frames into an in-memory ring buffer. Forwarder reads frames and rehydrates into OTLP for exporters.
3) Benchmark - microbenchmarks for encode/decode latency, allocation profile, and end-to-end export time under synthetic traffic.
4) Integration - route a % of traffic from Canary cluster to the compact forwarder. Observe SLI deltas and exporter correctness.
5) Rollout - ramp to 100% using canary steps with automatic rollback on error budget or elevated span loss.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Benchmarks show >=20% CPU saving and >=30% allocation reduction vs baseline. Attach benchmark logs to this ticket.
- No loss of mandatory span attributes for 99.99% of sampled spans when compact protocol is enabled.
- Unit and integration tests for encoder/decoder and fanout-throttle.
- Runbook: steps to disable compact protocol and switch back to legacy JSON forwarder within 5 minutes.

Monitoring & metrics to watch during rollout: 
- runtime: telemetry_export_cpu_seconds_total, runtime_heap_alloc_bytes_by_component (prometheus labels), process_gc_pause_seconds_count
- forwarder: compact_protocol_frames_in, compact_protocol_frames_err, forwarder_outbound_queue_depth, exporter_send_errors_total
- SLIs: span_ingest_success_rate, span_export_tail_latency_p95, span_export_cpu_per_span

Migration & compatibility: 
- Compact protocol is feature-flagged. Older forwarders will ignore frames and we will fallback to the JSON path. Deploy forwarder 1st then enable runtime encoder.
- Provide an emitter shim in the forwarder to translate any compact frames to existing OTLP pipelines for partner customers until they upgrade.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: subtle attribute delta-encoding bugs could lose attributes. Mitigation: conservative delta rules, end-to-end hashing/verification test that rehydrates frames and compares a sample set to the JSON output.
- Risk: increased complexity in forwarder causing regressions. Mitigation: keep new code behind a feature flag and maintain a simple fastpath in the existing forwarder for regressions.

Owner notes: engineering will partner with the SDK team for safe buffer pool implementations and with runtime performance team for kernel selection around memcpy hotpaths. Expect PRs in runtime repo and a companion repo for forwarder.

Related docs: RFC link in comments, benchmark artifacts and perf dashboards attached below.
